tools.name: myapi_status
tools.description:
CALL THIS FIRST on every new session. Verifies the ASC Ed25519 connection with a SIGNED probe (not just a key-existence lookup) and returns full operational context: identity, connected services, memory, and the API endpoint catalog. First-run setup, in priority order: (1) MYAPI_ENROLL_CODE (Quick Connect) — exchanges the one-time dashboard code for an instantly pre-approved key, zero further steps; (2) MYAPI_TOKEN — registers the keypair, user approves at https://www.myapiai.com/dashboard/devices. Either way the Ed25519 key becomes the permanent credential. Requires a paid plan (Pro or Heavy).

SCOPED ACCESS: this MCP is NOT master-token-only. Two least-privilege options:
  1. Register with a SCOPED token (MYAPI_TOKEN = a token with e.g. services:gmail:read):
     the Ed25519 key is permanently bound to those scopes server-side.
  2. Set MYAPI_AUTH_MODE=token: every request uses MYAPI_TOKEN as a plain Bearer
     credential (no key, no device approval for scoped tokens).
Either way, myapi_status reports the effective scope — respect it: 403s outside
the grant are expected, not errors to retry.

tools.name: myapi_request
tools.description:
Make any authenticated request to the MyApi API. Calls are signed with the ASC Ed25519 key (default) or sent with the Bearer token (MYAPI_AUTH_MODE=token). On 401 with asc_reason=device_not_approved, the MCP auto-restores and retries silently.

SCOPED CREDENTIALS: if myapi_status reported SCOPED access, only endpoints within the granted scopes work; everything else returns 403 by design. Check the scope list before calling, and surface missing scopes to the user instead of retrying.

⚠️ ALWAYS call myapi_status FIRST in a new session to verify the connection.
⚠️ If a request fails with an asc_reason you do not understand, call myapi_diagnose for a complete breakdown (clock skew, device status, plan).

KEY ENDPOINTS:
  GET  /gateway/context          — full context: identity + memory + services + endpoints
  GET  /identity                 — user identity (name, email, timezone, bio)
  PUT  /identity                 — update identity fields
  GET  /services                 — ALL services with status: native OAuth AND Composio-backed.
                                   Use the EXACT id from this list (e.g. gmail, notion, googlecalendar)
                                   — Composio services use their plain toolkit name, no prefix.
  GET  /services/{name}/methods  — documented operations for a service (call before first use)
  POST /services/{name}/proxy    — proxy any call to a connected service with body
                                   {path, method, body, query}. path = provider-native REST path.
                                   Works for native (e.g. /services/google/proxy) and Composio
                                   (e.g. /services/gmail/proxy) services alike.
  AFP — the user's OWN MACHINES (PCs/servers): file system + shell access.
  Use AFP whenever asked about the user's computer, server, docker, files, logs:
  GET  /afp/devices              — list registered machines (deviceId, name, platform, online)
  POST /afp/{deviceId}/exec      — run a shell command, body {cmd, cwd?, timeout?}
                                   e.g. {"cmd": "docker ps -a"} to check containers
  GET  /afp/{deviceId}/ls?path=  — list a directory;  /afp/{deviceId}/read?path= — read a file
  POST /afp/{deviceId}/write     — write a file, body {path, content}
  (AFP uses these direct routes — NOT /services/afp/proxy.)
  GET  /brain/knowledge-base     — user's knowledge base documents
  GET  /personas                 — AI personas defined by the user
  POST /memory                   — write a memory note that persists across sessions
  AUTOMATIONS — schedule proactive tasks MyApi runs on its own (Pro/Heavy plan):
  GET  /triggers                 — list the owner's automations
  POST /triggers                 — create one. Recommended shape:
                                   {name, kind:"schedule", schedule:{type:"daily",atHour:7,atMinute:0},
                                    timezone, actionType:"ai_prompt",
                                    action:{prompt:"plain-English task", services:["gmail","googlecalendar"]}}
                                   schedule.type ∈ once|interval|daily|weekly|monthly. ai_prompt runs an AI
                                   agent over the owner's CONNECTED services (it emails via their own mailbox).
  POST /triggers/{id}/run        — run an automation now (test); GET /triggers/{id}/runs — run history
  PATCH/DELETE /triggers/{id}    — edit / delete
  GET  /skills                   — available skills
  GET  /connectors               — OAuth connector status
  GET  /vault/tokens             — external API keys stored in the vault
  GET  /vault/credentials        — username/password credentials in the vault
  GET  /notifications            — user notifications
  GET  /export                   — export all user data

BROWSER-SESSION ENDPOINTS auto-rewritten to /identity for ASC: /auth/me, /users/me.
FORBIDDEN over ASC: /auth/login, /auth/logout, /auth/2fa/*, /auth/session-token, /oauth/*.

Do NOT prepend /api/v1 — it is added automatically.

path.description: API path starting with /. Do NOT include /api/v1.

tools.name: myapi_diagnose
tools.description: Diagnose why an ASC request just failed. Returns clock skew vs. server, signature validity, device approval status, plan, and a one-line next_action string telling the agent exactly what to do. Call this when you see any unexpected 401/403 from myapi_request — it eliminates guesswork.
